correctness.rationale: Reconstruction from the exact pair rule gives \(z_{k+1}=(1-2\mu)z_k\) and the signed mean increment \(\mu z_k\tanh(\lambda z_k/2)\). Absolute geometric bounds prove a convergent limit series and permanent confidence compatibility; positive summands and monotonicity prove a unique threshold. Geometric hyperbolic-tangent bounds prove both threshold endpoint scalings and a Riemann-sum limit gives the singular amplification coefficient. Exact strict rational integer inequalities certify the example. verify.py tests integer certificates, finite recurrences, tail bounds and numerical values, without using experiments to establish infinite-time claims.

value.rationale: The motivated invariant-range question is not just an isolated one-step violation: the result proves a sharp universal safety frontier for all positive utilities and finite populations, a unique two-parameter consensus-escape boundary in the natural exponential-utility subclass, critical curve endpoint laws, and a singular divergence of a convergent-pair consensus. This quantifies when shrinking interpersonal disagreement ceases to imply bounded consensus and identifies an actionable mathematical limitation of over-relaxed utility-weighted updating, without claiming empirical impact or stochastic classification.
